title: Cap. IX Resp. to Major's second confirmation: Christ obtained reconciliation for all — only individual impenitence bars participation
pass_a_gloss: Secondly they contend that no one is reprobated as considered only in the common sin of Adam, because Christ obtained reconciliation for all, of which that they may become partakers only the impenitence of singulars can stand in the way. They themselves untie the knot which they tied. For if by the very oblation of Christ applied, reconciliation or redemption were obtained for all and singular, some force would be in this argument: but as it is not applied to adults except by means of faith and actual penitence, so neither to infants except by means of supernatural Regeneration.
pass_b_english: Secondly they contend that no one is reprobated merely as lying in Adam's common sin, because Christ obtained reconciliation for all — and only each person's impenitence can bar them from sharing it. They untie the knot they tied. If reconciliation or redemption were obtained for every person by Christ's offering already applied, the argument would have some force. But as it is not applied to adults except through faith and actual penitence, so neither to infants except through supernatural regeneration.
source_text: Secundo contendunt neminem reprobari ut consideratum solummodo in communi Adae peccato, quia Christus omnibus reconciliationem impetravit, cujus ut fiant participes sola obstare potest impoenitentia singulorum. Ipsi solvunt nodum quem nexuerunt. Si enim ipsa Christi oblatione applicata reconciliatio sive redemtio omnibus et singulis esset obtenta, virium aliquid huic argumento inesset: sed sicut adultis non applicatur, nisi mediante fide et poenitentia actuali, ita neque infantibus nisi mediante Regeneratione supernaturali.
